:::{#def-epl}
#### Expected prediction loss at a covariate value

The **expected prediction loss at $\predvar$**
of a [fitted model](#def-fitted-model) $\fitted = \fitmodf{\trainset}$
is the expected [loss](#def-observation-loss) $\obsloss{*}\paren{\fitted}$
of the fitted model at a [new observation](#def-new-observation) $(\newpredvar, \newoutvar)$ with $\newpredvar = \predvar$.
The fitted model comes from a [fitting procedure](#def-fitting-procedure) $\fitproc$
applied to a random [training set](#def-training-set) $\trainset$ of $\nobs$ [observations](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-observation),
drawn independently of $(\newpredvar, \newoutvar)$,
so the fitted model is random.
The expected loss averages over $\trainset$ and over $\newoutvar$,
so its value depends on $\fitproc$ and $\nobs$:

$$
\epl{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar} \eqdef \E{\obsloss{*}\paren{\fitmodf{\trainset}} \mid \newpredvar = \predvar}.
$$ {#eq-epl}

:::

:::{#rem-epl-generalization-error}
#### The expected prediction loss and the generalization error

The [generalization error](#def-generalization-error) $\generr_{\trainset}$
holds the training set fixed and averages the loss over new covariate values too.
The expected prediction loss at $\predvar$ averages over training sets as well,
and holds the covariate value fixed.
Neither is the [test error](#def-test-error):
the test error is an average over a finite test set,
so it estimates the generalization error without equalling it.

:::
